text.brief: In Shanghai in February 1972, Richard Nixon approved a communiqué in which the United States acknowledged a position without adopting it.
text.record: The Shanghai Communiqué of February 28, 1972 states that the United States acknowledges that all Chinese on either side of the Taiwan Strait maintain there is but one China, and that it does not challenge that position ([American Institute in Taiwan: U.S.-PRC Joint Communique (1972)](https://www.ait.org.tw/u-s-prc-joint-communique-1972/); [State Department Office of the Historian: Rapprochement with China, 1972](https://history.state.gov/milestones/1969-1976/rapprochement-china)). The Chinese text renders the verb as renshi dao, which means to come to understand. The Chinese text of the 1979 normalization communiqué used chengren, the word for diplomatic recognition ([FRUS 1977-80 vol. XIII, doc. 186: memorandum on the Chinese text of the joint communique](https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1977-80v13/d186); [CRS report RL30341: China/Taiwan, evolution of the One China policy (everycrsreport mirror)](https://www.everycrsreport.com/reports/RL30341.html)). When senators raised the change in 1979, the administration answered that the English text governed ([CRS report RL30341: China/Taiwan, evolution of the One China policy (everycrsreport mirror)](https://www.everycrsreport.com/reports/RL30341.html)).
text.reading: The Party reads each American text through its own translation and then cites the translation as the American position, which is Stratagem 25. The Party works in the space between an American One China policy and its own One China principle, and each new text widens that space.
text.gapText: Data Architecture. Two governments kept two texts of one agreement, and nothing required the Party's text to carry the verb Washington chose.
text.fix: Publish the governing text of every joint statement in both languages, and answer each divergent rendering on the record.
